body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not always provide a minimum 12-month eligibility period for each child, as required by 98.21(a)(1). Hold public hearing. Hold public hearing. Attend the Joint Legislative Committee for Administrative Rules meeting. 09/30/2025 5 Rule changes are adopted. Review changes to rule with Bureau of Family Assistance’s Training Unit for updates to child care refresher trainings. Caseworkers are also informed of the rule changes through a Supervisory Release notification. 10/31/2025

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency did not consult with local child care program administrators prior to conducting a market rate survey or alternative methodology, as required by 98.45(e)(1). (Plan Question 4.2.1cii) • The Lead Agency does not sufficiently address the methodology used to complete the narrow cost analysis or estimated cost of care, the variations in analysis, assumptions and data included in the methodology, or consideration of higher-quality care, as required by 98.45(f)(1)(ii). (Plan Questions 4.2.2a, 4.2.2b, 4.2.2c, and 4.2.2d) Overall Target Completion Date: 02/28/2026 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 As the state approaches its next Market Rate Survey/Narrow Cost Analysis in 2026, it will ensure full compliance by… Market Rate Survey: Identifying key local child care program administrators to form a consultation group. Establishing regular provider communication channels around the MRS (e.g., quarterly meetings, email updates). Scheduling meetings and surveys to gather input on market rate survey, NCA or alternative methodology. Recording all feedback and integrate relevant insights into the survey process. Documenting formal procedures to consult stakeholders prior to conducting surveys. Training staff to implement these procedures effectively. Collecting feedback from stakeholders on the 02/28/2026 consultation process and improve as necessary. Narrow Cost Analysis: Assessing the existing narrow cost analysis, including assumptions, data sources, and quality considerations. Working with UNH Casey School of Public Policy for expert support. Providing clearer explanations of: Assumptions used in the analysis. Variations in cost analysis (e.g., geographic, program size). Higher-quality care cost considerations (e.g., wages, facilities, accreditation). Sharing methodology drafts with child care providers, administrators, and advocacy groups for feedback. Documenting the application of the revised methodology in reports. Reviewing the process annually and make adjustments as needed

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency standard for emergency preparedness and response planning does not include volunteer training or practice drills for licensed centers, as required by 98.41(a)(1)(vii). (Plan Question 5.3.7vi) • The Lead Agency does not require pre-service or orientation training on emergency preparedness and response planning for licensed centers, licensed family child care homes, license-exempt centers, license-exempt family child care homes, or license- exempt in-home providers, as required by 98.44(b)(1)(i). (Plan Question 5.4.1g) • The Lead Agency does not require an annual unannounced inspection for licensed centers for compliance with standards for emergency preparedness and response planning or with related pre-service or orientation training requirements. Additionally, the Lead Agency does not require an annual unannounced inspection for licensed family child care providers, or an annual inspection for license-exempt centers or license- exempt family child care providers for compliance with pre-service or orientation training requirements related to emergency preparedness and response planning, as required by 98.42(b)(2)(i)(B) and 98.42(b)(2)(ii). (Plan Questions 5.5.1aii, 5.5.1bii, 5.5.2ai, and 5.5.2bi) Overall Target Completion Date: 09/30/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 NH DHHS Child Care Licensing Unit completes rules-based inspections. Emergency preparedness and response training is listed in NH Administrative Rule He-C 6914 as a preservice/orientation requirement. 12/31/2024 2 NH Administrative Rule He-C 4002 will be revised to clarify that volunteers used as a staff person to meet child to staff ratios are required to complete emergency preparedness training and participate 09/30/2025 in drills. Once added to the rule, programs will be monitored for the requirement. 3 Due to edits in 2022 rule revision, the cross reference in the Emergency Operations Plan training requirements to the Emergency Operations Plan components inadvertently omitted communication and reunification with families. However, per He-C 4002.16(h), accommodations for infants and toddlers, children with disabilities, and children with chronic medical conditions is a required component of the response actions developed in the EOP in accordance with He-C 4002.16(g)(3), and the training requirement in He-C 4002.33(b)(14) specifies that training include the components in He-C 4002.16(g)(3). Therefore, NH respectfully disagrees that accommodations for infants and toddlers, children with disabilities, and children with chronic medical conditions is not covered as a required component of training in emergency preparedness. He-C 4002.16(g)(2) requires that EOPs include procedures for communications and reunification with families, and He-C 4002.16(j) requires that staff review EOPs within 30 days of hire. He-C 4002 is currently under revision and will specifically include communication and reunification with families as part of the training. Once added to the rule, programs will be monitored for the requirement. 09/30/2025 4 NH DHHS will identify edits to the individual requirements for emergency preparedness and response training to NH Administrative Rule He-C 6914. 12/31/2024 5 NH DHHS will review rule changes with the Department’s Administrative Rules Unit. Hold public hearing. Attend the Joint Legislative Committee for Administrative Rules meeting. 04/30/2025

body: Reason(s) for non-compliance: • The Lead Agency does not describe processes to train staff who administer the CCDF program and providers about program integrity, as required by 98.68(a)(3). (Plan Questions 10.1.5ai and 10.1.5bi) Overall Target Completion Date: 08/31/2025 Action Step Number Action Step Description Target Completion Date 1 Identify program integrity training for DHHS staff and enrolled providers will be created and implemented. Training for child care providers will be offered through Pro-Solutions with an expiration of three years so the training is completed for each renewal. (a) Lead Agencies are required to describe in their Plan effective internal controls that are in place to ensure integrity and accountability, while maintaining continuity of services, in the CCDF program.
